history.summary: Saivite Amman temple at Begampur, Dindigul, at the base of the Dindigul rock fort; its historical name is Dhandeeswaram. The Mariamman idol is traditionally said to have been installed by soldiers of Tipu Sultan's army at the fort, hence 'Kottai' (fort) Mariamman; the temple building itself was constructed later, reportedly ~200 years ago (exact date unverified). Square-plan temple on a ~2-acre campus with a small square sanctum in which the moolavar is embedded deeply under the floor - said to symbolise that everyone must bow before the goddess. Golden kavacham adorns the deity daily 5-9 PM. Other shrines include Vetri Vinayaka, Murugan, Kali, Durga, Madurai Veeran, Karuppusamy and Navagraha. Managed by a board of trustees. name: Kottai Mariamman Temple
town_description: Dindigul is a city in central Tamil Nadu, headquarters of Dindigul district, dominated by its 900-ft rock fort built in 1605 by the Madurai Nayak king Muthu Krishnappa Nayakar. The region sat at the border of the Chera, Chola and Pandya kingdoms and passed through Mysore, Hyder Ali and British rule; today it is known for locks, textile mills, tobacco and its temples.

travel.railway: Dindigul Junction (DG) on the Madurai-Trichy line, ~1-2 km from the temple
travel.road: On NH 44 (old NH 7) and the Chennai-Theni highway; located in the Begampur/West Car Street area of central Dindigul.

visitor_information.best_time: February-March for the Masi festival; October-March generally
